name: psk31
label: PSK31 (BPSK keyboard chat)
description: PSK31 is the most popular HF keyboard-to-keyboard mode: 31.25 baud binary phase-shift keying with a Varicode alphabet, occupying only ~60 Hz. Tiny power goes a long way — a ragchew QSO at 25 W is routine. On the waterfall it's a thin clean carrier with two faint sidebands; multiple QSOs stack a few hundred Hz apart in the sub-band. Decoded text streams under the decoder::fldigi log target (vendored fldigi PSK core). Tune so the signal sits ~1500 Hz in the USB audio (dial ≈ signal − 1.5 kHz); the modem's AFC locks the carrier. Activity clusters tightly: 14.070, 7.070, 3.580, 21.070, 28.120 MHz (±~3 kHz). Audio is teed alongside so you can listen.
ai_notes: PSK31 (BPSK 31.25 baud Varicode, vendored fldigi psk core). Watering holes (USB dial): 3.580 / 7.070 / 14.070 / 21.070 / 28.120 MHz — tune dial ≈ centre − 1500 Hz so the sub-band lands on the 1500 Hz PSK sweetspot; click into individual signals on the waterfall. Output: `tail decoder --category fldigi`. Bursty QSO traffic, not a beacon — wait for activity. psk63/psk125 modes also available via the Psk31Demod `mode` param.
